question: What is the term used to describe programs that distinguish between uppercase and lowercase letters, treating "yes" and "YES" as different inputs?
solution:
The correct answer is __Case-sensitive.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Case-sensitive__ programs treat uppercase and lowercase letters as distinct.
 
• For example, the input “yes” is different from “YES” in such programs.
 
• This feature is common in password fields and programming languages.
 
• Being case-sensitive ensures greater security and accuracy in data processing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Case-insensitive:**

 
 
• Programs that are case-insensitive treat uppercase and lowercase letters as equivalent.
 
• For example, “yes” and “YES” would be considered the same input.
 
 
 
• **Programming Languages:**
 
 
• Languages like Python and Java are case-sensitive.
 
• However, languages like SQL are case-insensitive by default.
